summary: N. Aiyaswami Sastri was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University. He served as Professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

N. D. Mironov (1880–1936) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig (~1901–1903) and under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1902–1903) and Hermann Jacobi (~1903–1905).

N. Lakshminarayana Rao worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and as Special Officer (Epigraphy) for the Government of India in 1956.

N. P. Chakravarti (1893–1956), a scholar of archaeology and Indology, studied at Calcutta, Paris, Berlin, and Cambridge (PhD). He held several epigraphy posts before serving as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950) and advisor (~1950–1952).
N. R. Bhatt (1920–2009) was an Indology scholar. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, where he was attested as a member in 1966.

N. S. Ramachandra Murthy is an Indology and archaeology scholar. He served as an Epigraphy Assistant in Andhra Pradesh (attested 1981) and later retired as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology at Sri Venkateswara University.

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya (1928–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Vice Chancellor of Rashtriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha (1989–1994) and was a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1994–2017).

N. Veezhinathan, an Indology and philosophy scholar, earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (-1964) studying under A. Sankaran. He held posts at Deccan College (1960–1963) and the University of Madras starting in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley. He served as Reader at the University of Madras (attested 1957) and Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh.

Nae Ionescu (1890–1940) was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912), University of Göttingen (~1913–1914), and University of Munich (~1915–1919), later holding a post at Bucharest (~1920–1938).
Nagin J. Shah (born 1931) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He succeeded Dalsukh Malvania and served as Acting Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) studied at Calcutta and London under scholars including Louis de La Vallée Poussin. In Buddhist studies and Indology, he taught at Judson College and Calcutta (~1924–1958) and served as Asiatic Society President (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir (born 1955), an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied under Colette Caillat. She held posts at CNRS, INALCO, Sorbonne Nouvelle, EPHE (Directeur d'Études from 2000), and the University of Paris (attested 2007).

Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr (attested 2004) and held an academic post at Carleton University (attested 2004).

Nam-lin Hur is a scholar of Japanese history, religion, and culture. He studied at Tokyo and Princeton (PhD under Helen Hardacre), completed a postdoc at Harvard, and became a professor at the University of British Columbia.

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and serves as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche (1931–2003) studied Buddhist and religious studies at Michigan, Jarvis Baptist Seminary, and under traditional teachers including Mahasi Sayadaw and the 16th Karmapa. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami (1906–2002) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), taught there (~1949–1967), and later served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Gauhati University under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

Namkhai Norbu (1938–2018), a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong, and Khamdre. He taught at Southwest Minzu University, IsMEO, and the University of Naples (1962–1992), and founded the Shang Shung Institute (1990).
